public_rationale: Under the output-capability reading, the categorical denial is contradicted. Before the post, researchers had demonstrated GPT-3 generating formal meaning representations, including without grammar-constrained decoding. Accuracy was imperfect, but the capability was measurable across held-out examples. This finding addresses the denial of structured representations; it does not challenge the statement about fluent prose. The verdict depends on reading the claim as an output-capability claim rather than a claim about the internal representations used during ordinary generation.
limitations: The experiments use task-specific examples and bounded semantic-parsing domains.
Correct execution of a generated representation does not establish general compositional understanding.
The alternative internal-representation reading remains unsettled by these records.

our_interpretation: The plain output-capability reading is that GPT-style models cannot generate readable representations of sentence meaning and its constituent relationships. Task-specific prompting counts; the claim does not require spontaneous output or perfect accuracy.
An alternative reading concerns interpretable internal representations used during ordinary generation. Successful semantic parsing does not establish that architectural claim.

The period is an as-of snapshot of models available by 2022-06-22. These capabilities have no regular reporting period, so the interval has no invented starting date and includes demonstrations already public before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Architecture documentation and representative evaluations establish fluent generation while showing that the contemporary models cannot produce usable structured sentence representations under the output-capability reading.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A contemporary GPT-style model demonstrably generates interpretable structured meaning representations across held-out utterances, including conditions where a separate parser does not supply the representation.
